extracted.intended_audience: researchers submitting preprints; volunteer recommenders/editors/reviewers; stakeholders interested in PCI's peer-review model
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for submitting, evaluating, and recommending preprints within the Peer Community In (PCI) network and publishing validated preprints in the Peer Community Journal (PCJ). Covers evaluation criteria (rigour, reproducibility), submission requirements (open data/code), and governance/ethical expectations (no financial conflicts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous evaluations by at least two reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions made by editors (called recommenders at PCI) are based on rigorous evaluations by at least two reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI states that editorial decisions are grounded in 'rigorous evaluations by at least two reviewers.' This is presented as a minimum standard for the review process and underpins recommendation decisions; speed and constructiveness are highlighted in testimonials but the formal requirement is two independent reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Board quality check and validation of editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Managing Board of each PCI, composed of established researchers who volunteer their time, checks the quality of reviews and validates all editorial decisions and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Managing Board acts as an oversight layer to ensure review quality and to validate recommenders' decisions, providing a governance check beyond individual recommenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open availability of evaluations (transparent peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: For accepted preprints, PCI evaluations are also publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is a core policy: PCI evaluations are published alongside accepted preprints, making the peer-review content accessible and supporting accountability and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of articles and associated data/code/scripts in open access repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles evaluated by PCI (preprints), as well as the associated data, code, and scripts, must be deposited in open access repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of PCI's embedding in Open-Science, submission/evaluation requires that preprints and their underlying materials be available in open repositories to enable verification and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of financial conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI prohibits financial conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preserve impartiality in review and recommendation, PCI explicitly forbids financial conflicts of interest for participants in the process (implicit for recommenders/reviewers), aligning with its reliability and ethics commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to justify sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI requires justification of the sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of reproducibility and methodological rigor, authors must provide rationale/justification for sample sizes in submissions; this is highlighted among PCI's quality policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on soundness of scientific questions
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI and Peer Community Journal focus their policies on the soundness of scientific questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation emphasizes whether the research question is well-posed and scientifically meaningful, rather than journal-based prestige metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on quality and reproducibility of results
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI and Peer Community Journal focus their policies on the quality and reproducibility of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and recommenders assess whether results are reliable and reproducible; policies encourage practices that support reproducibility (e.g., open data, scripts, sample-size justification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of preregistrations, Registered Reports, replication, and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI encourages the use of preregistrations and Registered Reports, the replication of studies and the publication of negative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practices are explicitly promoted as part of PCI's commitment to robust, unbiased science; they are recommended to authors and supported by PCI policies and infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of an author auto-questionnaire for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI provides to authors a detailed auto-questionnaire of evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The auto-questionnaire is a submission/support tool intended to guide authors through evaluation expectations and help reviewers assess key methodological and reporting elements (supports reproducibility and completeness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot data and script editing support (in selected PCIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI offers pilot data and script editing in two PCIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an active support measure, PCI provides hands-on help with data and script editing in pilot programs to improve reproducibility and the quality of submitted materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome standard: recommended preprints should be complete, reliable, and citable
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon positive evaluation, the PCIs validate and publicly recommend those preprints, making them complete, reliable, and citable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation is presented as a guarantee of scientific completeness and reliability, enabling authors to cite the preprint and to pursue publication in PCJ or other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoupling evaluation and publication; diamond open access publishing option
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI decouples evaluation and publication. An article recommended by a PCI may subsequently be published in Peer Community Journal (PCJ) — a diamond open access journal — or in any other journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model allows authors to keep the preprint on servers and choose publication routes; PCJ offers free OA publication for recommended articles, supporting access and removing author charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit, independent, free and open ethos guiding operations
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI and Peer Community Journal are non-profit, independent, free, and open; managed by scientists for scientists and embedded in Open-Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values shape procedural choices: minimizing costs, open-source infrastructure, free access for readers and authors, and governance by volunteer researchers—factors that affect how the review/publishing process is run and what is expected of participants.
